prize_parts.citation: for the development of palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: Pd-catalysed C-N coupling converted aryl amine synthesis from a harsh, narrow problem into a routine operation. Buchwald and Hartwig independently built general, ligand-controlled catalysts in the mid-1990s and then several generations of them (bulky biaryl phosphines, hindered alkylphosphines), supported by real mechanistic work on oxidative addition, amine binding and reductive elimination. The test I apply is whether a method is visible in countless later syntheses and in industry. Here it plainly is: Buchwald-Hartwig amination is among the most used C-N bond-forming reactions in pharmaceutical process and medicinal chemistry and in organic electronic materials. The work is over thirty years old, independently confirmed and not contested on priority between the two, and it extends the logic of the 2010 cross-coupling prize into a new bond type. Five of eight members ranked it, three of them first, which fits the chemistry, but my case rests on the chemistry and not on those counts.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is that the 2010 prize already honoured Pd cross-coupling, so this may read as an incremental sequel; I think the ligand design and the mechanistic understanding were new chemistry, not a substrate-scope extension, but the committee could reasonably weigh it differently. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling is a real precursor, and a citation that omits him will invite a priority argument. Hartwig also appears on other candidates, which could complicate how the committee treats him. Finally, a purely synthetic-methods prize is not the most dramatic option for the wider public, though that is not a criterion I would give weight to.

responses.point: Zou ranked B052 first and argues that Kosugi's tin-amide chemistry is a precursor but not the general method, so a two-person prize is cleanest. Zou also put the Gratzel/O'Regan dye-sensitised cell and the perovskite candidate second and third.
responses.response: I agree on Kosugi. His reaction needed toxic stannyl amides and had narrow scope. The general catalytic version with free amines and a base, plus the ligand classes that made it work, came from the two US groups, and a citation worded for the catalytic amination covers that point. I am less convinced by your B032 attribution. Miyasaka, Park and Snaith each have a claim, but Kanatzidis and Seok do too, and stability and lead toxicity are still open. That is where I would hold back, whereas for C-N coupling the question is only whether the committee wants a second cross-coupling prize.

responses.point: Linke, the chair, puts phase separation (B002) first as a thermodynamic framework for compartmentalisation, and ranks sequencing by synthesis (B035) second and B052 third. He accepts Buchwald and Hartwig as a clean pair.
responses.response: I respect the generality of the condensate concept, but I ask what was new chemically. Much of B002 is a cell-biology and soft-matter discovery. The decisive 2009 observation was imaging of P granules, and whether the cellular phenomenon is a true equilibrium phase separation is still argued, as Chabes also notes. I would not block a B002 prize but would not choose it ahead of a reaction that is used in industry every day. On B035, I agree that reversible-terminator chemistry is real chemistry, and it is mature. Its credit problem is serious, because Rothberg's pyrosequencing, Ju's terminators and Mayer's work all have claims and a Balasubramanian-Klenerman core leaves them out. I would take it more seriously if there were a way to word a citation around the chemistry.

responses.point: Chabes ranks base editing (B004) first as a clean chemical-mechanism story and targeted protein degradation (B037) second. He notes that clinical outcome data are still emerging and that approvals are pending.
responses.response: I put B004 seventh and B037 sixth, so we disagree on weight. Your point about clinical maturity is the same one that makes me cautious: for B037 no PROTAC drug is approved yet, and the chemical novelty seems to me to lie in the E3-ligand and ternary-complex chemistry (Ciulli's VHL work) and in the cereblon mechanism. For B004 the chemistry is a directed-evolution result, an adenine deaminase evolved to act on DNA, which I do see as new, but it sits close to the 2020 CRISPR prize. I agree there is real chemistry in both and I keep B037 as my first alternative, since its attribution can be reduced to Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli with some fairness. I would still rather reward something already proven over something whose payoff is still arriving.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks B052 first as a clear game-changer that extends 2010 into a new bond type, and ranks B037 second and B004 third. He finds three-name attribution in B037 difficult.
responses.response: I agree with the B052 reading and with the attribution problem in B037. Any three-name selection among Crews, Deshaies, Handa and Ciulli, plus Gray, Sakamoto and Kim, will be contested. Your split into Crews, Deshaies and Handa (concept plus the cereblon mechanism) is defensible, but it leaves out the medicinal chemistry that made degraders drug-like. If the committee wants B037 I would want to settle the citation wording first. For B052, your remark about Hartwig's appearance elsewhere is a minor point to me, since it does not change the two-person attribution.

responses.point: Sparr ranks condensates (B002) first and lipid nanoparticles (B045) second, as lipid and colloid physical chemistry with huge real-world impact, and ranks B052 fifth.
responses.response: I do not question the impact of B045, but the attribution is the problem, and your Cullis-Hope pairing differs from Anderson's and Langer's lipidoid line, which others favour. With six credited names and an overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize on delivery of modified mRNA, I do not see a defensible two or three-person prize yet. I would like you to say which discovery you consider decisive: the ionizable lipid, the rapid-mixing formulation or the lipid library. That would decide whether Cullis and Hope are the right pair. On B052 you ranked it fifth; I would ask what in particular you consider secondary, since I see the mechanistic ligand work as the part that is not incremental.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will treat C-N coupling as too close to the 2010 cross-coupling prize
Whether the citation should name Kosugi or be worded narrowly enough to leave his tin-amide precursor outside
Whether a prize with a biology-facing part (B002 or B037) should share with B052, which I currently do not prefer
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my provided profile for B052, B037 or B002. I have no known collaboration with Buchwald or Hartwig; my only link to the field is general, as a synthetic organic chemist who uses these methods, and I consider that insufficient for recusal.
